findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract now and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` now subclasses `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass`. That leaves the abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names` (processors/detector.py:142-144), `get_dedupe_value` (:150-156), `get_group_key_values` (:158-164) and the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data` (:166-170). `DetectorHandler` derives from `abc.ABC`, so `MetricAlertDetectorHandler(detector)` raises `TypeError`. It is bound to `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` (line 27), so `Detector.detector_handler` (models/detector.py:86) now raises for any detector whose type is `metric_alert_fire`. Before this diff the class returned `[]` from `evaluate`, so such a detector was a silent no-op. Nothing in the head creates detectors of that type (only the factory at src/sentry/testutils/factories.py:2133 creates `Detector` rows), so this is latent today. Fix: either keep this a non-stateful placeholder again, or implement the four abstract members for real.
findings.originReason: In the base, the class subclassed `DetectorHandler` and implemented `evaluate` by returning `[]`, so it could be instantiated.

verification.reason: `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` is now just `pass` on top of `StatefulDetectorHandler`. That leaves four abstract members unimplemented: `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. As a result, `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `Detector.detector_handler` raises `TypeError` for any `metric_alert_fire` detector. Nothing in the repo creates detectors of that type yet, so the bug is latent.

findings.title: build_mock_occurrence_and_event accepts `value` but never uses it
findings.body: The helper's `value` parameter (line 247) is not read anywhere in the body (lines 249-275). Call sites pass values that differ from the input, e.g. `test_results_on_change` feeds val1=100 (line 488) but expects an occurrence built with 6 (lines 489-491), and `test_dedupe` does the same with 8 (lines 508-511). These assertions pass regardless of the value, so the tests do not check what the name and arguments suggest. Either drop the parameter or pass the real value so the mismatch is visible.

verification.reason: The `value` parameter of `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` is never read in the body. Callers pass 6 while the evaluated packet holds 100 or 8, so the argument suggests a check the tests never make.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: The docstring says `evaluate` "returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`", but the signature (lines 226-228) and the body (lines 237, 243-244) now return a dict keyed by group key. Update the docstring to match.

verification.reason: The docstring still says `evaluate` returns a list. The signature and body now return a dict keyed by group key.

contracts.action: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is instantiated by Detector.detector_handler for a detector of type metric_alert_fire
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11-12 before this diff: DetectorHandler subclass whose evaluate returns []
contracts.before_after: Before: instantiation succeeds and evaluate returns an empty list, so the detector is a no-op. After: instantiation raises TypeError because four abstract members are not implemented.
contracts.visible_effect: None in the head: no code path creates a Detector with type metric_alert_fire. If one exists, process_detectors fails on it.
contracts.failure_mode: TypeError raised from Detector.detector_handler, which propagates out of process_detectors (processors/detector.py:53) and aborts evaluation for every detector in that call. Not caught.

contracts.action: New non-OK branch in evaluate_group_key_value calls build_occurrence_and_event_data and then the result is produced to Kafka
contracts.equivalent_path: src/sentry/spans/consumers/detect_performance_issues/message.py:52-57, the sibling call to produce_occurrence_to_kafka that passes occurrence, event_data and is_buffered_spans
contracts.before_after: Before: the non-OK branch set result=None, so no occurrence was produced. After: the subclass builds an IssueOccurrence and event_data, and process_detectors (lines 60-62) produces it via create_issue_occurrence_from_result. The sibling builds the occurrence and event_data itself before calling produce. The new path skips any event_id consistency check; the producer enforces it at src/sentry/issues/producer.py:100-101 and raises ValueError.
contracts.visible_effect: Occurrence reaches the issue platform through the Kafka producer. No user-facing effect while process_detectors has no callers in src.
contracts.failure_mode: If build_occurrence_and_event_data raises, or the producer raises ValueError on mismatched event ids, the exception leaves process_detectors before commit_state_updates (line 68). Dedupe and state are then not committed, so the next run re-produces results already sent for earlier group keys in the same call (at-least-once). The failure is not caught and is visible only as a worker exception.

contracts.action: Detector.group_type property is added and detector_handler now reads it
contracts.equivalent_path: The inline registry lookup that detector_handler did before this diff (same grouptype.registry.get_by_slug(self.type) call)
contracts.before_after: Same registry lookup, moved into a property. The None-check and the logger.error branches are unchanged.
contracts.failure_mode: None: the property returns None for an unknown slug, and detector_handler keeps its existing error logging and None return.

contracts.action: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns a dict keyed by result.group_key, and the duplicate-key error log in process_detectors is removed
contracts.equivalent_path: The list-returning evaluate and duplicate-check loop that process_detectors had before this diff
contracts.before_after: Before: list result, with a logger.error and skip on duplicate group_key. After: dict result. Duplicates are no longer detectable, because get_group_key_values returns a dict keyed by group key, so each key yields at most one result.
contracts.visible_effect: None. Only process_detectors and the tests consume this value; no other caller in src.
contracts.failure_mode: A custom handler could return a dict whose key differs from result.group_key, and process_detectors ignores the key and iterates values. No error is logged, but nothing in the head implements such a handler.

summary: Four files reviewed. The main problem is in src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now a StatefulDetectorHandler with an empty body, so it cannot be instantiated and any metric_alert_fire detector would raise TypeError. No code in the head creates such detectors, so this is latent. One test is wrong: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with group key "val1" while the call uses "group_key", so the frozen-dataclass equality fails. Also flagged: a helper parameter that is never used, a stale docstring that still says evaluate returns a list, and a stale TODO. process_detectors has no callers in src, so the new occurrence path has no user-visible effect yet. I did not run the tests; the test failure is established by reading the code.

entries.title: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds its expected occurrence with the wrong group key
entries.reason: `IssueOccurrence` defines its own `__eq__`, which compares only `id`. The dataclass decorator does not replace an `__eq__` already defined in the class body. Both occurrences use the hardcoded id `eb4b0acf...`, and the `event_data` dicts do not depend on the group key, so the different fingerprints do not make the assertion fail.
